newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African PPI seen falling further in May.
newsitem.headline: S.African PPI seen falling further in May.

text.p: South African producer price inflation should decline further to an annual rate of 8.2 percent in May, following a surprisingly large fall to 8.8 in April from 9.6 in March, according to stockbroker Huysamer Stals.

Economist Johan Roussouw said on Tuesday he now expected a 0.64 percent month-on-month rate of increase in May, with the imported component likely to increase 0.8 percent and locally-produced 0.6 percent.
"We beleive that the PPI inflation cycle has reached its upper turning point, and expect it to decline sharply to about 6.0 percent towards year-end," he said.
The average PPI rate in 1997 was likely to be 8.2 percent, against 6.9 percent in 1996, he added.
April's all-commodities producer price index rose 0.4 percent month-on-month and 8.8 percent year-on-year, far better than the consensus of 0.9 and 9.5 forecast by economists.
The low rate of increase reflected a sharp 3.2 percent monthly decline in the imported component, due to a big drop in crude oil prices.
